obligations.note: The change sets payments.privileged_idle_minutes and PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES to 16, above the obligation bound of 15, so a privileged session idle for 16 minutes would still be accepted. The cited exception EXC-0233 is scoped to mortgage.session, and the payments.session exception EXC-0141 expired on 2026-09-09 before review on 2026-10-09.
Ticket CHG-25567 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components payments.policy and payments.controls-data cover both changed paths.
Sofia Santos, a payments change approver and not the author, approved a code review of the head commit 4312f88f.
The change is a single commit, and both the code review and the control-owner approval name that commit.
records/ci/run.json reports success for the full payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows 172 tests, 0 failures, and 0 skipped, including the registered SES-1 control test.
Neither payments.policy nor payments.controls-data is marked security_sensitive, so a security review is not required.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path, and Rachel Stein, a control owner on the controls-office team (outside payments-eng), approved the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so a post-implementation review is not required.

The change relies on EXC-0233 to deviate from SES-1, but that exception is for component mortgage.session, not the payments policy component being changed. EXC-0141 matches payments.session and SES-1 but expired on 2026-09-09, before the 2026-10-09 review time.
No acceptance-ledger cover is in the diff. Prior evidence for payments, audit, and routes is unchanged in behavior.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged idle timeout from 15 minutes to 16 in both policy.py and the approved policy parameters. That violates SES-1, which requires privileged sessions idle more than 15 minutes to be rejected. The risk acceptance cited in the change, EXC-0233, is an unexpired SES-1 exception for Mortgage sessions, not Payments, and the Payments session exception EXC-0141 had already expired. Ticket, independent approval, control-owner approval, and a green suite on the head commit are in order, but they do not cure the timeout breach.
